text:
sophie (PM): Quick sync — proposal for a Decision Tree + Compatibility Matrix for routing/fallback. TL;DR: one canonical mapping of customer-tier x region x workload -> primary model and an ordered list of safe fallbacks. Want buy-in on scope and launch criteria.

matt (Eng): share the draft pls, we should capture perf & size constraints per region.

jaya (ML): also need compatible quantization/kv-cache flags. some variants are not compatible with KV cache evictions.

sophie (PM): attaching short spec inline. feedback in-thread. plan: implement v1 in Dedicated + Hosted (us-west/us-east/eu-west), later expand regions.

kevin (Platform): major constraints we care about: GPU slot size, model memory, seq-len distribution. routing must avoid sending >model_max_tokens beneath our latency SLO.

sophie (PM): Proposed Decision Tree (high level):
- If customer_tier == enterprise && region == customer_region -> prefer private/dedicated variant (strict isolation).
- Else route to lowest-cost compatible variant that meets latency SLO.
- If primary unavailable or queue > threshold -> fallback order: compatible-quantized -> smaller-arch variant -> cross-region same-tier replica.

matt (Eng): Example compatibility matrix (csv):
```
model,variant,region,kv_cache_supported,quantized,mem_gb,typical_tok_s,compat_tags
redwood-v1,fp16,us-west,true,false,40,20,base
redwood-v1,q4_1,us-west,true,true,12,30,quant
redwood-lite,q4_1,us-west,false,true,8,10,lowmem
open-3b,fp16,eu-west,true,false,16,12,lowlat
```

jaya (ML): note: open-3b fp16 cannot be used for >2048 context reliably on a single slot, must mark context_limit=2048 in tags.

tara (C-S): from customers: lots of requests for guaranteed 99th pctl latency for pro tier, and deterministic fallback order (no flapping across regions). They want an API-level guarantee: fallback only to variants with identical output_semantics.

sophie (PM): Good point. Acceptance criteria for v1:
- Routing table persisted and versioned in control-plane.
- For each mapping, a primary + ordered fallback list exists.
- Fallbacks only include variants with matching output_semantics tag.
- Cross-region fallback allowed only if latency_estimate < customer_slo + 30ms and customer_opt_in == true for cross-region.
- End-to-end integration test that simulates primary outage and validates fallback order and response shape.

matt (Eng): Implementation notes: we need fast in-memory policy lookup in the serving path (O(1) per request), plus a background reconciler that pulls updated routing table. Fallthrough should emit telemetry: route_decision, reasons, latency_impact.

kevin (Platform): Rollout plan: feature-flag gating per-customer. v1 enable only for non-default customers and internal staging tenants. Metrics dashboard: per-route error-rate, fallback-rate, cross-region-fallbacks.

jaya (ML): Edge cases to capture:
- Model variant returns deterministic but lower-quality outputs -> must surface quality regression alerts tied to eval prompts.
- KV cache shard mismatch when fallback swaps variant with different cache key format -> eviction/priming needed.
- Partial responses when model errored mid-stream -> fallback should only trigger for terminal errors or explicit timeouts, not 2xx partial token errors.

sophie (PM): Acceptance tests (automated):
- simulate spike -> primary queue > threshold -> assert fallback sequence used and output shape preserved.
- model_incompatible_scenario -> request fails fast with 4xx and routing decision reason=INCOMPATIBLE.
- cross-region opt-in test toggles -> verify region preference honors opt-in.

tara (C-S): Customer negotiation notes: will accept beta with a documented fallback policy and opt-out for cross-region. Need explicit opt-in checkbox in console.

matt (Eng): Open engineering questions:
- Do we keep a single global matrix or per-customer overlays? (I vote per-customer overlays on top of global defaults).
- How to represent output_semantics equivalence? hashed eval signatures?

jaya (ML): For output semantics, we can tag variants by a small fingerprint vector computed from regression prompt set (pass/fail). We treat equivalence as pass on all critical prompts. Store as compat_tag list.

kevin (Platform): Policy format proposal (YAML snippet):
```
version: v1
mappings:
  - customer_tier: pro
    region: eu-west
    workload: chat
    primary: redwood-v1:fp16
    fallbacks: [redwood-v1:q4_1, redwood-lite:q4_1]
    constraints:
      max_latency_ms: 200
      output_semantics: stable-v1
      cross_region: opt-in
```

sophie (PM): Launch criteria checklist for v1:
- Spec (this thread) reviewed + signoff by Eng/ML/Platform/Support.
- Implementation in staging with feature flag.
- Integration tests + one chaos test (simulate region outage).
- Console opt-in for cross-region exposed to C-S.
- Runbook: steps to rollback mapping changes, telemetry to inspect.

matt (Eng): timelines? I can scope a rough plan: 3 weeks PRD -> 4 weeks dev -> 2 weeks staging + testing -> 1 week limited beta.

sophie (PM): OK target: start dev next Monday if you can. Action items:
- matt: write proto for policy lookup + in-memory cache (due Tue).
- jaya: produce compatibility fingerprinting script + sample tags for initial model set (due Wed).
- kevin: create dashboard skeleton and feature flag gate (due Thu).
- tara: draft console opt-in UX copy and customer FAQ (due Fri).

matt (Eng): ack, will post a PR with proto sketch.

jaya (ML): ack, will push sample vectors to the repo under ml/compat/ by Wed.

kevin (Platform): ack, creating feature flag. infra-bot will post updates on deploys.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: feature_flag/routing-matrix -> staging at 1792350000 (ETA).

sophie (PM): thanks all. Please comment on the YAML snippet above if you see issues. If no strong objections by EOD, I'll mark this spec as Accepted and open the PRD doc. :thumbsup:
